claims.text: The starting precursor consists of tungsten particles dispersed in a copper matrix or mixed with copper powder, without surface modification.
A thin vapor-deposited nickel interlayer can be applied to tungsten particles before spark-plasma sintering.
The nickel interlayer modifies the surface energy of tungsten particles.
Modification of tungsten surface energy by the interlayer improves copper wettability during sintering.
Improved copper wettability reduces interfacial void formation.
Improved copper wettability reduces phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
The interlayer produces better contact at W–Cu metal–metal interfaces.
The interlayer leads to a more uniform distribution of tungsten and copper.
Reduced void content and improved interfacial contact increase the composite's thermal conductivity.
Reduced void content and improved interfacial contact increase mechanical integrity or durability.
Ni-coated W–Cu composites will have fewer voids than otherwise comparable composites produced from uncoated tungsten particles.
Ni-coated W–Cu composites will have higher thermal conductivity than otherwise comparable composites produced from uncoated tungsten particles.
Ni-coated W–Cu composites will have greater mechanical strength than otherwise comparable composites produced from uncoated tungsten particles.
The coating will remain intact and effective under the proposed spark-plasma-sintering conditions.
The interlayer will not compromise the composite's high-temperature stability or mechanical robustness.
